result.question: Discuss the political organisation of the Vijayanagara Empire with special reference to the amara-nayaka system. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: Founded by the brothers Harihara and Bukka in the fourteenth century, Vijayanagara grew into an empire stretching from the river Krishna to the extreme south of the peninsula.
Its rulers, called rayas, came from four successive dynasties: the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu.
Krishnadeva Raya, its most famous ruler, belonged to the Sangama dynasty.
He also wrote the Amuktamalyada, a work on statecraft, in Kannada.
The amara-nayaka system, probably derived from the iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate, was a major political innovation.
Amara-nayakas were military commanders who governed territories granted by the raya and collected taxes from peasants, craftspersons and traders.
They kept part of the revenue to maintain horses and elephants for the king and sent him tribute every year.
Kings occasionally controlled them by transfers, yet many nayakas rebelled and later became independent.
Rivalry with the Deccan Sultanates ended in defeat at Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota) in 1565, after which the capital was sacked.
Vijayanagara shows how delegated military power can both strengthen and weaken a state.
